data.actual: The shared presentation exports handlesControl and handleControlClick, but ssjpInstall only records installed state and adds no click binding. productionSharedJourneyEntry re-enables the legacy controls while the presentation owns them. leagueWheel.js and clubAssignment.js retain direct click listeners on the same controls. Targeted review of the loaded entry, identity, Showdown UI, football visual and V10 club modules found no external caller of the shared dispatcher. The written repro scans all js files to challenge that conclusion.
assumptions: The production path is the online shared path owned by productionSharedJourneyEntry and productionSharedShowdownPresentation.
No unexamined runtime dynamically delegates these controls; the repository-wide repro is written specifically to disprove this assumption when executed.
No prior olympiad report existed on qa/bug-olympiad at run start, so the lowest-coverage tie selected area 01.
disproof_attempts: Checked productionSharedShowdownPresentation: activate refreshes, renders and starts polling; ssjpInstall has no event binding.
Checked productionSharedJourneyEntry, onlinePlayerIdentity, showdownUI, footballVisuals, data/footballVisuals and clubScreenV10 for calls to handleControlClick or handlesControl; none were found.
Confirmed leagueWheel.js binds #spinLeague directly to handleLeagueWheelAction.
Confirmed clubAssignment.js binds #openClubPack to assignClubs and #continueClubAssignment to continueToShowdownHome.
Checked hunt-1017, hunt-1018, hunt-1019 and factory/gameplay-v1 BOARD.json; no duplicate of this control-ownership defect was found.
This chat cannot execute the repository repro, so the finding stays likely until its whole-js scan runs.
data.expected: While the shared presentation owns setup, each handled control press is routed once to the shared dispatcher and the legacy local draw handlers do not run. The provider remains the only league and club authority.

fix.change: While shared setup is active, install one capture-phase delegate for the handled control ids, dispatch to ssjpHandleControlClick, and consume that event before legacy target listeners execute. Remove or inert the delegate when the shared presentation deactivates.
fix.test: In a two-manager browser run, press the real league, club-pack and final-confirm controls. Assert one shared provider transition per press, zero local random draw authority, and matching phase on both devices. Run repro/chat-1006-0418-1.cjs as a source-wiring guard.

data.player_hurt: Both managers can be unable to advance a fresh shared Showdown because the coordinator can press a control that is still attached to the local draw path while the remote Shared Setup remains on the earlier phase.
data.root_cause: The shared presentation takes over labels, disabled state and rendering but not click ownership. The reused controls already have legacy listeners from gameplay initialization, and the local draw lock is removed once presentationActive() becomes true.
steps: Start a fresh shared Showdown, pair Daniel and Nik, and reach an exact ACTIVE private session.
Enter the polished shared league wheel so the shared presentation is active and the league action is enabled.
Press the league action once on the coordinator device.
Check whether the press is exclusively routed to CareerModeProductionSharedShowdownPresentation.handleControlClick or reaches leagueWheel.js handleLeagueWheelAction.
Repeat on the club-pack action and check whether clubAssignment.js assignClubs receives the press.
Compare local selectedLeague/clubs with the provider Shared Setup phase on both devices.
symptoms: The shared league control can change only the coordinator's local league while the rival remains on the previous remote setup phase.
The club-pack control can enter the local club assignment path instead of the provider-bound draw.
One phone can appear to advance while the other keeps waiting.
The journey can fail to reach Career Start until the authoritative transition is performed by some other path.
data.title: Shared league and club controls are unlocked without wiring the authoritative click dispatcher

data.actual: The provider hashes the private normalized guess payload together with operation metadata, then publishes both that hash and every non-private hash input in the rival-readable public ledger. A one-slot guess has only 200 possible values, so it is recoverable in at most 200 hashes. Across three optional slots the full space is only 201^3 = 8,120,601 candidates.
assumptions: The production deployment uses the generated Rules source that includes firestore.transfer-challenge-production.fragment.rules, as configured by deploy-firestore-rules-zero-billing.yml on this main revision.
An entitled rival is treated as adversarial within their own authenticated browser; privacy must be enforced by stored data and Rules, not by hiding DOM controls.
One locked guess is a valid protocol state, so the 200-candidate case is reachable without malformed input.
disproof_attempts: Checked the role-document Rules: opponent role documents are correctly unreadable before public phase COMPLETED, but this does not protect the public operationHash.
Checked the public transfer Rules: entitled rivals are explicitly allowed to get the whole public document, including operationIds, operationTypes, operationHashes, baseRevisions and actorRoles.
Checked whether the random operationId makes brute force impractical: it is public in the same ledger, so every hash input except guesses is known.

Checked whether SHA-256 preimage resistance is sufficient: the guess domain is deliberately tiny, 36 leagues plus 164 nationalities per occupied slot, so exhaustive candidate verification is practical.
Checked earlier olympiad findings, hunts 1017/1018/1019 and BOARD.json; none reports this low-entropy public-hash privacy leak.
data.expected: Before COMPLETED, the rival can learn only public phase/lock metadata; the values of private guesses must not be testable or recoverable from rival-readable data.

fix.change: Do not expose a deterministic private-payload commitment whose verification inputs are all public before COMPLETED. Keep the payload hash/nonce in the actor's private role document, or salt the payload with a cryptographically random nonce that remains private until reveal, while retaining a public receipt that excludes private guess values.
fix.test: In the Firestore emulator, lock one and three guesses as one manager. As the rival, read every document the Rules permit before COMPLETED and exhaust the complete 36-league/164-nationality catalog against any public receipt. No candidate must be verifiable; after COMPLETED both managers must still receive the same revealed guesses and verdict inputs.

data.player_hurt: Nik or Daniel can have locked private guesses recovered by the rival before the Transfer Challenge reaches COMPLETED.
data.root_cause: A deterministic unsalted SHA-256 commitment to the low-entropy private guesses is stored in a public document. operationId acts like a salt in the hash input but is published beside the hash, so it adds no secrecy.
steps: Start a shared Transfer Challenge and reach GUESS_ENTRY.
Have playerOne lock exactly one valid league or nationality guess.
As playerTwo, read the public transferChallenges/season_N document; production Rules allow any entitled manager to get it.
Take the lock-guesses operationId, operationType, operationHash, baseRevision and actorRole from the public append-only operation arrays.
Enumerate the 36 league IDs plus 164 nationality IDs for the locked slot and SHA-256 the exact canonical command shape used by stspMutate.
Stop when a candidate hash equals the public operationHash. The matching candidate is playerOne's private guess even though the public phase is not COMPLETED.
symptoms: A rival can recover a one-slot private guess essentially immediately after it is locked.
The UI and role-document Rules still hide the rival's private card/document, creating a false privacy boundary.
The same deterministic commitment exposes low-entropy information before the intended reveal phase.
data.title: Public operation hashes let the rival brute-force private guesses before reveal

data.actual: The Rules accept any 2-to-80-character lowercase hyphenated option ID and any 1-to-80-character signing name. The provider reader instead requires exact membership in the repository's canonical league/nationality sets and requires signing names to equal their trimmed form. Therefore rule-valid data can be provider-invalid. Once public phase is COMPLETED, stspRead loads both role documents and returns a provider error instead of verdicts.
assumptions: An entitled manager can use or modify the same browser Firestore client that the app uses; Firestore Rules, not UI code, are the authorization/integrity boundary for direct client writes.
The production deployment composes firestore.transfer-challenge-production.fragment.rules into its active Rules source, as verified in the preceding area-02 run.
The example fake league ID is absent from the repository canonical league catalog; the repro checks this against data/transferOptions.js.
No server-only mutation gateway sits between the production browser provider and these transfer documents; sparkSharedTransferChallenge uses client Firestore transactions.
disproof_attempts: Checked the normal production UI and provider path: transfer selectors produce canonical IDs and stspNormalizeSignings rejects unknown league/nationality IDs and untrimmed names, so ordinary taps are safe. That does not protect the Firestore security boundary from a modified authenticated client.

Checked the Rules around the private/public atomic lock: they enforce actor role, active session/device authority, timestamps, slot uniqueness, public phase transition and public/private linkage, but ssjrTransferValidOptionId never checks the 36-league or 164-nationality allowlists and the signing-name rule never checks trim equality.

Checked completed-read behavior: before COMPLETED the rival role document stays unreadable, but at COMPLETED stspRead explicitly rereads with readOpponent=true and stspPrivateState invokes the stricter catalog normalization, so the malformed payload is no longer avoidable.
Checked simultaneous normal final locks: production retries one stale/permission race and converges to COMPLETED, so the ordinary race itself is not the defect.

Checked earlier olympiad findings, hunt-1017, hunt-1018, hunt-1019 and factory/gameplay-v1 BOARD.json. Hunt 1019 confirms that the provider rejects unknown catalogs, but none of those reports identifies the weaker Firestore Rules validator or the rule-valid/provider-invalid persisted state.

This chat run cannot execute the Firestore emulator, so the finding remains likely. The written Node repro statically proves the validator disagreement and is intended to be followed by an emulator write in Work mode.
data.expected: Every private transfer payload that production Firestore Rules permit must satisfy the same canonical catalog and normalization contract as the normal provider reader. A non-FIFA league or nationality ID, or a signing name the reader would reject as untrimmed, must be denied before it becomes shared authority.

fix.change: Make the Firestore transfer validators enforce the same canonical league and nationality ID sets and the same trimmed-name invariant as sparkSharedTransferChallenge. Generate or otherwise maintain exact allowlists from the canonical transfer catalog, then regenerate the composed production Rules through the existing Rules workflow.
fix.test: In the Firestore emulator, as an entitled manager with a valid active session/device, attempt direct lock-signings transactions with a fake slug-shaped league ID, fake nationality ID and an untrimmed player name; each must be denied. A canonical control signing must be accepted, and two normal final locks must still reach COMPLETED with identical readable verdicts on both manager accounts.

data.player_hurt: A validly authenticated manager can commit syntactically valid but noncanonical transfer signing data that Firestore Rules accept; when the challenge reaches COMPLETED, the normal shared reader rejects that stored role document, so both managers can lose the verdict reveal and be unable to continue the Showdown.
data.root_cause: The production Firestore Rules model canonical transfer IDs as a generic slug shape and signing names as only a length-bounded string, while the browser provider treats exact FIFA 17 catalog membership and trimmed names as invariants when reading authority. The write boundary is therefore weaker than the read boundary.
steps: Run a shared Transfer Challenge normally until both managers have locked canonical guesses and the public phase is SIGNING_ENTRY.

On the manager who will lock signings first, bypass the normal provider helper but stay authenticated on that manager's active account, device and private session. Submit the same atomic public lock-signings transition plus that manager's private role update, but put a slug-shaped leagueId that is not one of the 36 FIFA 17 transfer league IDs, for example definitely-not-a-fifa17-league.

Keep every other field rule-valid: preserve the locked guesses, use a valid nationality ID, valid slot/name/timestamps, append the public operation metadata, and satisfy the current actor/session/device linkage.
The production Rules accept the fake leagueId because their option validator checks only slug syntax and length, not membership in the canonical FIFA 17 catalog.

On the other manager's untouched client, lock normal canonical signings. The public transaction advances the challenge to COMPLETED because the rival private payload is still unreadable before completion.

Allow the normal post-lock refresh to read the completed challenge. It now must read both private role documents; sparkSharedTransferChallenge normalizes the poisoned signing against the real catalog and rejects the read.
symptoms: A malicious or modified authenticated client can poison its own signing role document while the public ledger records a valid signing lock.
The honest rival can still perform the second signing lock because SIGNING_ENTRY reads only the honest manager's private payload.
The public ledger can reach COMPLETED while the normal completed projection is unreadable because it now requires the invalid opponent role document.
Further transfer mutations are blocked by the completed public phase, leaving the verdict/season-results handoff stuck unless remote data is repaired.
The same validator mismatch also permits an untrimmed signing name that Rules accept but the provider rejects.
data.title: Firestore Rules can accept transfer inputs that the normal reader rejects

map: Entry: START A SHOWDOWN is intercepted by online identity and productionSharedJourneyEntry; a fresh local shell is created only after identity/storage prerequisites and is marked sharedJourney.setupPending.
Authority gate: shared setup requires the exact connected account, registered device, attached Daniel/Nik rivalry and unexpired ACTIVE private session before provider reads or mutations.

Remote state: Shared Setup advances through empty/open, LEAGUE_WHEEL_COMMITTED, CLUB_ASSIGNMENTS_COMMITTED, SEASON_LENGTH_COMMITTED and SHOWDOWN_CONFIRMED; provider protocol owns deterministic league and club draws.

Local state: the shell starts with selectedLeague=null and empty clubs; the shared setup contract intentionally does not mutate canonical local league/club fields while remote setup is being established.

Presentation: productionSharedShowdownPresentation reuses #spinLeague, #openClubPack and #continueClubAssignment, relabels/locks them from remote state, animates the authoritative league and club results, and exposes handleControlClick for mutations.

Legacy writes: leagueWheel.js and clubAssignment.js still bind direct click handlers that generate and save local league/club choices; productionSharedJourneyEntry removes its local-draw lock when the shared presentation reports active.

Timers: local wheel uses a 4 s reveal; local club reveal uses 650/1750/2850/3300 ms stages. Shared presentation uses a 4 s league animation, 4.2 s auto-forward, 650/1750/3000 ms pack stages, visibility deferral, and polling.
Awaits/races: shared setup refreshes coalesce, mutations serialize, stale/permission races re-read and retry once, and presentation actions have their own actionPromise guard.
data.next_focus: Area 02: trace transfer timer authority and private guess secrecy across simultaneous start/end, reload, expired session, offline recovery and cross-device polling.
premortem: Most likely: reused setup buttons keep their legacy local click handlers while the shared presentation only changes their appearance/state, so a visible shared tap does not advance remote authority. This survived review and became chat-1006-0418-1.

Reload or backgrounding during league/club reveal could strand a device before confirmation. Disproof: authoritative phase is reread, reveal witnesses reset by context, hidden-tab league forward is deferred until visible, and pack animations restart from remote state.

Host/peer ordering or double taps could duplicate a draw or leave different remote revisions. Disproof: only coordinator transitions draw phases, presentation serializes actions, provider mutations serialize, and stale/permission races re-read/retry against immutable provider-bound draws.

map: Entry: shared seasonPrimaryAction is intercepted in capture phase by productionSharedTransferChallenge, which refreshes authority before navigating to transferChallenge; legacy transfer button handlers are stopped for shared controls.

State: one public season-scoped transferChallenges/season_N ledger carries phase, revision, timer timestamps, lock-role lists and operation receipts; each manager has a separate roles/{managerRole} private document for guesses/signings.

Writes: coordinator start creates the public ledger; each early-end request or timer expiry updates public state; lock-guesses atomically appends a public operation receipt and creates/updates only the actor's private role payload.

Privacy projection: sparkSharedTransferChallenge reads only the actor private role before COMPLETED; production UI hides the rival guess/signing card. Production Rules likewise gate rival private-role get until public phase COMPLETED.

Public authority: the deployed Rules path is generated from firestore.spark.rules plus production fragments; the transfer fragment allows an entitled rival to get the entire public transfer ledger, including operationIds, operationTypes, operationHashes, baseRevisions and actorRoles.

Timer: display ticks every 1 second from public startedAt plus 15 minutes using a forced Firebase ID-token issuedAtTime anchor and performance.now; server clock is refreshed every 5 minutes and reset on visibility return.
Expiry: client calls advanceExpiredWindow at displayed zero, but production Rules independently require request.time >= stored startedAt + 15 minutes, preventing an early client-clock advance.

Polling: normal refresh is 15 seconds; a waiting manager gets 3-second reads for up to 3 minutes; expiry writes retry after 30 seconds. Hidden tabs suspend transfer polling/timer work and refresh on visibility return.
Concurrency: mutations are serialized through providerChain and guarded by busy; stale/permission race codes re-read and retry once, with special convergence handling for simultaneous expiry.

Await boundaries: dependency loading, Setup refresh, Career Start refresh, account services, server-clock token refresh, provider read, provider transaction and post-start refresh all carry an exact save/rivalry/season request key before rebinding view.

Targeted support reads disproved a false Rules finding: production deploys generated Rules containing the transfer fragment, not root firestore.rules alone. Targeted session snippets also showed the UI preflight rejects an already-expired held session; the broader expiry/reconnect scope is already represented by hunt 1018/job 31.

Surviving privacy failure: lock-guesses hashes the private normalized payload deterministically, while the same rival-readable public ledger exposes every other hash input. The repository catalog is only 36 leagues plus 164 nationalities.
data.next_focus: 03: trace signing locks through atomic private/public writes, check whether signing receipts leak unrevealed payloads, verify reveal completeness and league-or-nationality verdict semantics, then attack simultaneous final locks and reload after only one manager has locked signings.
premortem: Private guesses leak before reveal through public/shared metadata even though rival role documents and cards are hidden. Tested first; survived as chat-1006-0441-1.

The two devices disagree on the 15-minute deadline or advance the window early after reload, clock skew, sleep or simultaneous zero. Server request.time expiry enforcement, post-start refresh, monotonic display clock and visibility resync disproved the early-advance path; offline recovery remains dependent on reconnect.

Double taps, simultaneous early-end/expiry, or one device acting one phase ahead strands the other or duplicates a lock. busy/providerChain plus append-only revisions, role lists and one stale-race retry cover the ordinary races examined; known session-expiry recovery defects were deduplicated against hunt 1018/BOARD job 31.

map: Entry and controls: productionSharedTransferChallenge captures the shared Transfer Challenge controls before legacy listeners and sends only the active manager's private guesses/signings through the provider.
State: public transferChallenges/season_N records phase, revision and lock receipts; each manager's guesses/signings live in a separate roles/{managerRole} private document.

Signing lock: sparkSharedTransferChallenge performs the actor private-role write and public signingLockedRoles/phase update in one Firestore transaction; the second signing lock changes public phase to COMPLETED.

Reveal: before COMPLETED reads include only the actor's private role; at COMPLETED the provider rereads in the same transaction with readOpponent=true and requires both role documents to normalize successfully before producing verdicts.

Verdict: a signing is RELEASE when at least one rival guess matches either its canonical previous-league ID or its canonical nationality ID. Multiple matching guesses still produce one release decision.

Concurrency: production serializes mutations, blocks local double taps and retries one stale/permission race; after a competing final lock it treats COMPLETED or the actor already being locked as convergence and refreshes.

Reload/waiting: role payloads and public lock state are remote authority; waiting signers poll every 3 seconds for up to 3 minutes then every 15 seconds, with hidden tabs refreshing on visibility return.

History: completed transfer history later requires every season's public ledger and both private roles and recomputes public operation-hash provenance; transfer-history unavailability is kept separate from career points/trophies.

Rules boundary: production Firestore Rules enforce atomic role/session/device linkage and transfer phase deltas, but their option validator checks only slug shape while the provider reader requires exact FIFA 17 catalog membership and trimmed signing names.

Surviving failure: an entitled modified client can therefore create rule-valid/provider-invalid signing authority; the honest rival can make the final lock, after which the completed reveal must read the poisoned opponent role and fails.
data.next_focus: 04: trace seasons 2 to 10 and the next-season step end to end: accepted-season gating, cursor advancement, double continue, reload/offline between seasons, transfer-state reset, season 10 boundary and 1-season immediate terminal behavior.
premortem: Most likely: simultaneous final signing locks race and one device gets stranded. Disproof: the provider transaction rejects the stale loser, production rereads once, recognizes an already-locked/COMPLETED outcome and refreshes the full completed projection.

Reload after only one manager locks signings loses that manager's private payload or reopens editing. Disproof: the private role document and public signingLockedRoles persist independently of page memory, and rendering disables the locked actor after the authoritative read.
A write accepted by Firestore can violate the provider's canonical signing contract and poison reveal. Tested against the Rules/provider validators; this survived as chat-1006-0503-1.

data.next_focus: If area 04 is checked again, inspect the shared season commit handoff into multi-season progression, especially season 9 to 10 and the terminal transition.
